4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 1

My daily routine

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn the verbs of a normal day (los verbos del día a día)
  • Say what you do in order with first, then, after that
  • Use time words: in the morning, in the afternoon, at night
  • Talk and write about your own routine

Para pensar

Si un niño de Londres te pregunta «What do you do every day?», ¿qué le contarías? ¿Hay palabras que ya sabes decir?

Explicación

What is a routine?

A routine is something you do every day, more or less at the same time. You wake up, you have breakfast, you go to school… Your routine is like the timetable of your day.

En castellano: una rutina es lo que haces todos los días, casi siempre en el mismo orden. En inglés decimos daily routine («rutina diaria»), porque daily viene de day (día). Para hablar de ella usamos el presente: «I get up», «I brush my teeth». Es igual que en español cuando decimos «me levanto» o «me lavo los dientes».

Morning verbs

These are the verbs of the morning. Say them aloud: wake up (despertarse), get up (levantarse), have a shower (ducharse), get dressed (vestirse), brush my teeth (lavarse los dientes), comb my hair (peinarse) and have breakfast (desayunar).

Look: wake up and get up are different. First you open your eyes (wake up), then you get out of bed (get up). Many routine verbs have two words: get + up, get + dressed. Learn them together, like a pair of shoes.

At school and in the afternoon

Then the day goes on. I go to school (voy al cole), I have lessons (tengo clases) and I play with my friends at break time (en el recreo). At two o'clock I have lunch (como).

In the afternoon I go home (vuelvo a casa), I do my homework (hago los deberes) and maybe I go to the park or I go swimming. Ojo: en inglés decimos do homework, no make homework. Y para las comidas usamos have: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner.

In the evening and at night

At the end of the day we slow down. I have a bath (me baño), I have dinner (ceno) with my family, I watch TV or I read a book. Then I put on my pyjamas (me pongo el pijama) and I go to bed (me voy a la cama).

When you go to bed, you say «Good night!». En castellano: no confundas good evening (buenas tardes, al llegar a un sitio por la tarde) con good night (buenas noches, para despedirse o irse a dormir). ¡Y recuerda dormir unas diez horas, que tu cuerpo está creciendo!

Saying the time of your routine

To say when you do something, use at + the time: «I get up at half past seven», «I have lunch at two o'clock», «I go to bed at nine».

For the parts of the day we use other little words: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night. En castellano: «a las ocho» es at eight; «por la mañana» es in the morning. Fíjate que en inglés no se dice «at the eight»: la hora va sin the.

Putting things in order

When you tell your routine, use order words (palabras para ordenar): First, I get up. Then, I have a shower. After that, I have breakfast. Finally, I go to school.

These words help the listener follow your story, like the steps of a recipe. Consejo: después de First, Then y After that se pone una coma. Puedes repetir then varias veces, pero queda más bonito si alternas con after that y next.

How often? Always, usually, never

Some things you do every day, and some things you do only sometimes. We use frequency words: always (siempre), usually (normalmente), sometimes (a veces) and never (nunca).

They go before the verb: «I always brush my teeth», «I sometimes go to the park», «I never go to bed at midnight». En castellano: igual que «siempre me lavo los dientes». Y para todos los días decimos every day, al final de la frase: «I read every day».

Reading: Lucía's day

Read Lucía's text: «Hi! I'm Lucía and I'm nine. On school days I get up at half past seven. First, I get dressed. Then, I have breakfast: milk and toast. I go to school by bike with my dad. At school I have lunch at two o'clock. In the afternoon I do my homework and I play with my dog, Rufo. I have dinner at eight and I always read a comic in bed. I go to bed at half past nine.»

Answer: What time does Lucía get up? How does she go to school? What does she read in bed?

Your turn: my routine poster

Make a routine poster. Fold a big paper into six squares. In each square draw one moment of your day and write a sentence under it: «I get up at eight», «I have breakfast», «I go to school»…

Then, present it to the class with order words: «First… then… after that… finally». Your classmates can ask: «What time do you get up?». Consejo: repasa que cada frase empiece por I (siempre en mayúscula) y que uses at delante de la hora.

My daily routine

Ejercicios

  1. Translate: levantarse, vestirse, desayunar.

  2. Translate: hacer los deberes, cenar, irse a la cama.

  3. Complete: «I ___ my teeth every morning.»

  4. Complete with in, at: «___ the morning I have a shower ___ half past seven.»

  5. Order: «I / get up / always / at seven».

  6. What is the opposite of «always»?

  7. Write the order words: primero, luego, después de eso, por último.

  8. Correct: «I make my homework at five.»

  9. What do you say when you go to bed?

  10. Write three sentences about your morning.

Practica

  1. «Levantarse» in English is…

    1. A) get dressed
    2. B) go up
    3. C) get up

  2. «Desayunar» is…

    1. A) have breakfast
    2. B) have dinner
    3. C) have lunch

  3. «I ___ my homework.»

    1. A) make
    2. B) do
    3. C) have

  4. «I get up ___ seven o'clock.»

    1. A) in
    2. B) at
    3. C) on

  5. «___ the afternoon I play.»

    1. A) At
    2. B) On
    3. C) In

  6. Which word means «nunca»?

    1. A) never
    2. B) always
    3. C) usually

  7. Which is an order word?

    1. A) every day
    2. B) at night
    3. C) after that

  8. «I ___ brush my teeth.» (siempre)

    1. A) sometimes
    2. B) always
    3. C) never

  9. «Cenar» is…

    1. A) have dinner
    2. B) have lunch
    3. C) go to bed

  10. What do you say before sleeping?

    1. A) Good night!
    2. B) Good evening!
    3. C) Good morning!

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué es una rutina diaria; Los verbos de la mañana, la tarde y la noche; Cómo decir la hora de cada acción con at e in; Las palabras para ordenar y las de frecuencia.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

daily routineRutina diaria: lo que haces cada día.
get upLevantarse.
get dressedVestirse.
have breakfastDesayunar.
do my homeworkHacer los deberes (con do).
go to bedIrse a la cama.
at + horaat eight = a las ocho.
always / neverSiempre / nunca (delante del verbo).

Soluciones

  1. C) get up.
  2. A) breakfast = desayuno.
  3. B) do homework.
  4. B) Horas con at.
  5. C) In the afternoon.
  6. A) never.
  7. C) Sirve para ordenar.
  8. B) always = siempre.
  9. A) dinner = cena.
  10. A) Para dormir: good night.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. get up, get dressed, have breakfast.
  2. do my homework, have dinner, go to bed.
  3. brush.
  4. In, at.
  5. I always get up at seven.
  6. never.
  7. first, then, after that, finally.
  8. I do my homework at five.
  9. Good night!
  10. Model answer: I get up at eight. I get dressed. Then I have breakfast with my sister.
